# 1\. LAB OVERVIEW

## 1.1  Why This Lab Exists

Dynatrace stores logs, metrics and traces in Grail and queries them with one language, DQL. Engineers who can filter logs, summarise errors and chart a metric in a few lines answer "what exactly failed, how often and how bad" without leaving the platform.  
In this lab you work only in your browser. You search the easyTravel logs in the Logs app, run three DQL log queries in a duplicated personal Notebook, chart host and service metrics with timeseries, and save a personal dashboard that reuses your queries.

| 🎯  NIIT iRUN Alignment |
| :---- |
| INCIDENT OWNERSHIP: You can find the exact failing log line and count it per service or process. |
|  |
| TROUBLESHOOTING EXCELLENCE: You will combine logs and metrics with the same time window to confirm a failure. |
|  |
| OPERATIONAL READINESS: You can turn a useful query into a reusable dashboard tile. |

## 1.3  Conceptual Foundation

DQL is a pipeline: fetch data, filter it, aggregate it, then show it. Learn the commands you use today.  
*Figure: DQL Pipeline — fetch logs / timeseries → filter → summarize / makeTimeseries → sort → limit → Notebook Section or Dashboard Tile*

| Command | Does | Example | Result |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| fetch logs | Reads log records in a timeframe | fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h | Raw log lines |
| filter | Keeps matching records | filter loglevel \== "ERROR" | Only errors |
| summarize | Aggregates by fields | summarize errors \= count(), by: {dt.process.name} | One row per process |
| timeseries | Reads a metric over time | timeseries avg(dt.host.cpu.usage) | A line chart |

*Figure: Logs and Metrics Together — The Same Two-Hour Window: Error Count Rises While Response Time Rises*

# 3\. CONCEPT DEEP-DIVE BEFORE STARTING

## 3.1  Logs, Metrics and DQL in Grail

OneAgent sends logs and metrics to Grail. DQL reads both: fetch logs reads log records, timeseries reads metrics. Because they live in one store, one Notebook can show the failing log lines and the metric that moved at the same time, with one time filter.

| 💡  Why This Matters Operationally |
| :---- |
| A saved query is a reusable answer: the same DQL can become a Notebook section or a dashboard tile. |
|  |
| Always bound the time (from: now() \- 2h) — unbounded queries are slow on a shared tenant. |

## 3.2  The Critical Distinction: Notebook vs Dashboard

A Notebook is for investigating: you run queries, read results and write notes. A dashboard is for monitoring: tiles refresh automatically and are shared. Develop a query in a Notebook first, then promote the useful ones to a dashboard tile.

| ⚠️  Most Common Mistake When Writing DQL |
| :---- |
| A learner runs fetch logs with no time filter and no limit on a shared tenant and waits minutes for millions of rows. |
|  |
| REASON: DQL scans everything in the default window unless you narrow it. |
|  |
| YOU MUST add a time filter (from: now() \- 2h), filter early, and use limit while exploring. |

## 3.3  DQL Quick Patterns

| Goal | Pattern | Used In | This Lab |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Find error lines | fetch logs \| filter loglevel \== "ERROR" | Logs app / Notebook | Tasks 1–2 |
| Count by group | summarize count(), by: {field} | Notebook | Task 2 |
| Metric over time | timeseries avg(metric) | Notebook / tile | Task 3 |
| Keep a result | Add as dashboard tile | Dashboard | Task 4 |

| 📝  How to Decide Logs App or DQL |
| :---- |
| Ask: "Do I want to read lines or count them?" Reading and filtering lines → Logs app. Counting, grouping, charting or reusing → DQL in a Notebook. Then promote the best query to a dashboard tile. |

| **1.A  Paste one error line (time and content) and name the process or host that wrote it.**  Answer: Nov 20, 06:58:18.000 — ERROR \[HeadlessVisit\] Cannot click element \[\[ChromeDriver: chrome on LINUX ...\]\] (container: dynatrace/easytravel-headless-loadgen, EC2 instance: i-0ef42f2c086dcd3e1). |
| **1.B  Which attribute lets you jump to the trace, and what would break that link?**  Answer: The trace\_id (or dt.trace\_id) attribute lets you jump to the distributed trace via the "View trace" button. That link breaks (or is disabled) when logs are emitted outside a traced HTTP request context (such as container/headless loadgen or OS logs), when W3C trace-context headers (traceparent) are missing/not propagated across services, or when trace sampling/retention drops the trace.  |

| 2 | Summarise the Errors with DQL in Your Notebook*Dynatrace Logs, Metrics & DQL SOP — Day 2 — Lab 2* | ⏱ 6 min |

DQL counts and groups what the Logs app only lists. You duplicate the shared \[TEMPLATE\] Notebook, name it Lab7-\<YourName\>, and run three log queries.

| :---- |

| \# Step 2 (UI): New DQL section → run:  errors per process |
| fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| filter loglevel \== "ERROR" \| summarize errors \= count(), by: {dt.process\_group.detected\_name} \| sort errors desc ![][image7] |
|  \# Step 3 (UI): New DQL section → run:  the latest CreditCardCheckError500 lines |
| fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| filter contains(content, "CreditCardCheckError500") \| sort timestamp desc \| limit 10 \| fields timestamp, loglevel, content  ![][image8]  |
| \# Step 4 (UI): New DQL section → run:  errors over time |
| fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| filter loglevel \== "ERROR" \| makeTimeseries errors \= count(), interval: 5m ![][image9] |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| Table: one row per process with an error count, the easyTravel backend process on top |
| Table: up to 10 recent lines with timestamp, ERROR and the CreditCardCheckError500 text |
| Line chart: error counts per 5 minutes, higher while the fault is on |
| **2.A  Record the top process and its error count, and the time the errors peaked.**  Answer:  The top process was Linux System with 445 errors (followed by amazon-ssm-agent with 8 errors), and the error rate peaked around 06:00 AM during the 04:49:01 – 06:49:01 window. |
| **2.B  Why does the query start with fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h, and what would change if you removed the time filter?**  Answer:  Starting with fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h restricts the Grail query scan to the active 2-hour incident window; removing the time filter forces DQL to scan historical log data across the tenant, making the query significantly slower and mixing older, unrelated errors into the results.  |

| **3.A  Describe the CPU line and the response-time lines (level, rise, time).**  Answer:   Host CPU (avg(dt.host.cpu.usage)) maintains a baseline level of roughly **20%–35%** across the 2-hour window (05:23:00 – 07:24:00), with periodic spikes reaching **\~73%** around **06:09 AM** and **\~74%** around **06:58 AM**. Service response time (dt.service.request.response\_time) returns **0 records** (No records) across the window because full-stack JVM/service-level OneAgent injection and the CreditCardCheckError500 fault plugin are inactive on this personal trial tenant.  |
| **3.B  Do the metric and log charts agree about when the problem started? Explain.**  Answer:  On a full-stack tenant with an active service fault, the error log spike and service response-time rise occur in the exact same time window. On this personal tenant, dt.service.request.response\_time has no ingested data to show a service slowdown, while the recorded ERROR logs (453 total, peaking around 06:00 AM) originate from host/OS (Linux System, amazon-ssm-agent) and headless browser loadgen (dynatrace/easytravel-headless-loadgen) activity—though periodic host CPU spikes (such as \~74% at 06:58 AM) align with those container/loadgen execution bursts. |

| **4.A  Describe your tile (query, visualisation) and why you chose it.**  Answer:  The tile runs fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| filter loglevel \== "ERROR" \| summarize errors \= count(), by: {dt.process\_group.detected\_name} \| sort errors desc rendered as a Table (or Bar chart) over the Last 2 hours timeframe. I chose this query and visualization because grouping and sorting ERROR logs by process immediately highlights which component is driving the highest failure volume (Linux System with 445 errors vs. amazon-ssm-agent with 8 errors) at a single glance. |
| **4.B  When would you promote a Notebook query to a dashboard, and when keep it in the Notebook?**  Answer:  Promote a query to a Dashboard when it tracks recurring health indicators, SLA/error-rate KPIs, or high-level operational views that teams need to monitor continuously or share across stakeholders. Keep a query in a Notebook during active incident investigation, ad-hoc exploration, root-cause correlation across raw log lines and metrics, or when documenting step-by-step troubleshooting notes alongside live query outputs. |

# 6\. TROUBLESHOOTING — COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Issue / Error | Cause | Diagnosis | Fix |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| DQL: query returns no rows | Time filter or field name wrong | Run fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| limit 10 to see fields | Check field names (loglevel, content) and widen the timeframe |
| Permission error saving | You edited a shared object | Check the name of the Notebook or dashboard | Duplicate the shared object and save your copy |
| Notebook runs slowly | No time filter or no limit | Look for from: now() \- 2h | Add the time filter and limit while exploring |
| No metric line for a service | Wrong metric key or entity filter | Remove the by: clause and rerun | Use the metric key from the quick reference; ask the instructor |
| Process name column empty | Field not present on these logs | Open one log line and read its attributes | Group by another attribute shown in the log detail (host, service) |
| Dashboard tile empty | Tile timeframe differs from the dashboard | Compare the tile and dashboard timeframes | Set the dashboard timeframe to Last 2 hours |

## 7.2  Common Mistakes — Learn From These

| Mistake | Why It Happens | Consequence | Prevention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No time filter | Defaults differ | Slow query, mixed data | Use from: now() \- 2h every time |
| Editing the template | Looks like your copy | Breaks it for 40 learners | Duplicate first |
| Wrong field names | Guessing | Empty result | Read one log line's attributes first |
| Charts with different windows | Different tile timeframes | Wrong conclusions | Use the same window everywhere |
| Dashboards with raw logs | Easy to add | Slow, noisy dashboards | Show counts, rates and top-N |

# 10\. QUICK REFERENCE — DYNATRACE LOGS, METRICS & DQL COMMAND CARD

Bookmark this page. Every path and DQL pattern you need in SOP order.

| Category | Path / DQL | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Open tenant | https\://qcw66226.live.dynatrace.com | Shared tenant |
| Logs app | Ctrl/Cmd \+ K → Logs · loglevel \= ERROR | Read lines |
| Errors per process | fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| filter loglevel \== "ERROR" \| summarize errors \= count(), by: {dt.process.name} | Count by group |
| Latest failing lines | … \| filter contains(content, "CreditCardCheckError500") \| sort timestamp desc \| limit 10 | Evidence |
| Errors over time | … \| makeTimeseries errors \= count(), interval: 5m | Trend |
| Host CPU | timeseries avg(dt.host.cpu.usage), from: now() \- 2h | Metric |
| Response time | timeseries avg(dt.service.request.response\_time), by: {dt.entity.service}, from: now() \- 2h | Metric by service |
| Notebook | Notebooks → \[TEMPLATE\] → Duplicate → Lab7-\<YourName\> | Personal copy |
| Dashboard | Dashboards → \[TEMPLATE\] → Duplicate → Lab7-\<YourName\> → Add tile | Personal dashboard |
| Time filter | from: now() \- 2h — always | Shared tenant |
| Read-only rule | Edit only your own copies | Shared tenant |
| Promote | Notebook query → dashboard tile | Reuse |

# APPENDIX A — INSTRUCTOR PRE-CLASS RUNBOOK (5 MINUTES BEFORE COHORT)

Instructor only. The runbook takes about 5 minutes; run it before the cohort. Learners never see or run these commands.

| ⌨  Appendix A — Instructor pre-class runbook (EC2 ip-172-30-0-220, 5 minutes before cohort) |
| :---- |
|  |
| \# Step 1: Enable the CreditCardCheckError500 plugin so error logs and metrics change, then switch it off again |
| export FAULT\_MINUTES=20 |
| curl \-s "http\://localhost:8091/services/ConfigurationService/setPluginEnabled?name=CreditCardCheckError500\&enabled=true" |
| (sleep \$((FAULT\_MINUTES\*60)); curl \-s "http\://localhost:8091/services/ConfigurationService/setPluginEnabled?name=CreditCardCheckError500\&enabled=false") & |
|  |
| \# Step 2 (UI, as a Cohort-40 test user): Logs app → loglevel \= ERROR, Last 2 hours → lines must be present |
| \# Step 3 (UI): Run the three DQL log queries and the two timeseries queries of Tasks 2–3 in a test Notebook; check that \[TEMPLATE\] Notebook and \[TEMPLATE\] dashboard exist and can be duplicated |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| HTTP 200 from the plugin call |
| Within a few minutes ERROR lines with CreditCardCheckError500 appear in the Logs app |
| All queries return rows; the templates duplicate without a permission error |

| ⚠️  INSTRUCTOR ONLY — Notes for 40 Concurrent Learners |
| :---- |
| Verify before class: Cohort-40 may create Notebooks and Dashboards but not edit shared ones; the field names loglevel, content and dt.process.name exist on these logs; the metric keys dt.host.cpu.usage and dt.service.request.response\_time return data. |
|  |
| The DQL field and metric names are examples taken from standard Grail data; adjust them (and the quick reference) if your tenant differs. If the fault ends before class, run Step 1 again. |
